about: The widow's bedroom as meshy_room_build.py builds it for the first-person walk: the room's own choices (the wall colours, the door and the window, the night outside, where every piece stands, the stills' views). The builder reads this file for --scene widow_bedroom; its load_room explains the keys. Colours are sRGB hex. Positions are metres in the room's frame: x east, y north, z up, the floor's centre on the origin. A key named note, or <key>_note beside <key>, is a comment: the builder drops it. The room checks keep their own numbers for this room in tools/blender/room_checks/rooms/widow_bedroom.json; the two files are merged in a later step.
wall_colour_note: a muted sage drab: never pink or lilac under the candle and the moon
wood_colour_note: the joinery's dark brown mahogany (the scan's grain on this colour)

meshy.note: the village's own Meshy models in place of the boxes and cones; a house is [model, u, d, size, turn]

moon.note: from straight out of the window, toward its wall's +s side

exposure_note: null: chosen from the bake (the builder's choose_exposure)
layout_note: The arrangement. `pieces` and `views` are the room as it is built by default, `bed_north`: the owner's first-person layout (2026-11-16, "Move it"): the bed's head against the north wall under his photographs, its foot to the south; wardrobe_body turned in its corner to stand against the east wall (the north wall free, an aisle beside the bed); the candle stand beside the bed's head, in the nook between the washstand and the bed; the chest at the bed's foot; the photographs raised as a group over the head board. The 2.5D game keeps its own map. `layouts` holds the other arrangements as overrides by piece id (a piece's keys replaced whole) and by view name: `mapped` is the room as the game's map has it (built until 2026-11-15: the bed free in mid-room, the photographs 1.8 m north of it), kept buildable with --layout mapped.

pieces.note: its doors shut here: ajar (as in `mapped`) they would cut the 0.86 m aisle beside the bed to 0.65 m
the press's open door is the upper one at its south end (door2): door1's leaf, at its north end, would stand in the mouth of the aisle beside the bed
6 cm west of the photographs' old centre (x 2.5), and they with it: at 2.5 the aisle between the coverlet and wardrobe_body was 0.80 m to the centimetre
raised 0.28 m: the two small frames clear the head board's crest (1.26 m) by 0.16 m, the three ovals the head posts' tops (1.68 m) by 0.11 m, the group's top 0.17 m under the picture rail

this piece and the two after it are the first person's dressing (decor: not in the scene's props; locked Poly Haven models, real size): her tub armchair on the west wall (at y 0.5 it is whole in the spawn's view and between two tile centres: at y -1.5 its arm was cut by the frame's corner), a nightstand with the mantel clock in the south-west corner, a settle on the south wall. Each stands against its wall and leaves part of every walkable tile open.

views_note: name: [eye x, y, z], [target x, y, z], the vertical field of view in degrees. The eye's 1.6 m and the 70 degrees are the walk viewer's own (the builder's EYE and VFOV).

views.bed_note: the bed, the candle and his photographs
views.press_note: the linen press and the room in front of it
views.photos_note: from the bed's foot, over the chest
